speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help me diagnose your condition, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of diabetes and the progressive weakness, have you noticed any specific patterns, such as symptoms worsening at night, dropping objects, or difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning a shirt?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The combination of progressive muscle weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes alongside sensory symptoms and a history of diabetes strongly suggests a neurodegenerative process like ALS. Given the severity of the motor signs, I need to confirm the diagnosis with specific imaging and lab work.
